knowledge_point.title: Computing an Integral Using the Sum Rule

question.:question/worked-solution:
Applying the sum rule, we compute the sum of the integrals of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \left(3-x^{3}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x &= \int \left(3-x^{3}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x \\ &= 3\int 1\,\mathrm{d}x-\int x^{3}\,\mathrm{d}x \\ &= 3\frac{x^{0+1}}{(0+1)}-\frac{x^{3+1}}{(3+1)}+C \\ &= 3x-\frac{x^{4}}{4}+C\end{aligned}
$$
